steps.observation: You have 900 seconds. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
Here are three high-leverage strategies cities can use to cut carbon emissions:

1. Electrify and Optimize Urban Mobility  
   • Expand frequent, reliable public transit (BRT, light rail) and dedicated bus/bike lanes  
   • Support electric-vehicle adoption with charging networks and low-emission zones  
   • Incentivize walking, cycling and shared micro-mobility (e-scooters, bike-share)  

2. Boost Building Efficiency and Low-Carbon Construction  
   • Tighten energy-performance standards for new builds (passive-house, net-zero codes)  
   • Retrofit existing stock with better insulation, high-efficiency HVAC and smart meters  
   • Mandate low-carbon materials (cross-laminated timber, recycled steel) and on-site renewables (solar PV, heat pumps)  

3. Decarbonize Energy Supply and Urban Infrastructure  
   • Procure or generate renewable electricity (community solar, wind, geothermal)  
   • Modernize grids with energy storage, demand-response and distributed microgrids  
   • Electrify heating via district heat networks or heat-pump systems, phasing out fossil fuels  

Each of these approaches not only drives down CO₂ but also improves air quality, public health and resilience.
